clue.text: Throw oneself into exercises without a breather

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
the organ you breathe with

explanation.surface: Someone launches into a workout without pausing for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking, and 'a breather' is an organ rather than a rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunge is to dive headlong, committing yourself fully to an activity.

clue.text: Criticise girl for releasing the evils of the world?

definitions.text: for releasing the evils of the world?
definitions.note: a description of the answer, the woman who released them

blocks.note: to pan is to review harshly
a girl's name

explanation.surface: Blaming a woman for unleashing all the world's ills.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is close to an &lit: the girl to be criticised is the myth's heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pandora opened the jar, or box, that let sickness and misery loose on humankind.

clue.text: Marry a French female without sex appeal

indicators.note: without means outside, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: feminine form of a in French
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone weds a Frenchwoman who lacks allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside. 'It' as sex appeal is 1920s slang, from the film star Clara Bow, the It girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite two people is to join them, as marrying joins a couple.

blocks.note: surface reading: a sneak who informs on others
setter's reading: the official in the story of William Tell

explanation.walkthrough: Tell-tale means the tale of William Tell, the Swiss archer.
explanation.definitionFit: In the legend the Austrian bailiff ordered Tell to shoot an apple off his son's head, and was later killed by him.

clue.text: Still used as a name for a US lake

definitions.text: a name for a US lake

blocks.note: first meaning: calm, untroubled

blocks.clueFragment: a name for a US lake
blocks.note: second meaning: Lake ... in New York State

explanation.surface: Something calm is said to lend its name to an American lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Placid, in the Adirondacks of New York, hosted two Winter Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and undisturbed, as still water is; it is also the name of a well-known lake.

clue.text: Willingly left member with account to pay finally

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: something left in a will

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before

blocks.note: a limb
standard abbreviation
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone happily walked out leaving a bill to be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willingly' puns on 'by will', so 'willingly left' is property bequeathed. The 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is money or property bequeathed in a will to someone after death.

clue.text: Potentially fierce sea battle avoided by this

indicators.note: potentially means what the letters could become, a different arrangement

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A truce that heads off a possibly savage naval engagement.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceasefire is a halt to shooting agreed by both sides, which prevents further fighting.

clue.text: Strangely, when there's more than one they become high

definitions.text: Strangely, when there's more than one they become high

blocks.clueFragment: Strangely, when there's more than one
blocks.note: surface reading: some oddity of number
setter's reading: in the plural the open ocean is called the high seas

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that something deep turns high once plural: the open ocean far from land is called the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: The deep sea is the ocean far below the surface, the open water where the high seas lie.

blocks.note: plain reading: the strongest urge in one's character
setter's reading: a tyrant's desire is literally to rule

explanation.walkthrough: The plain sense is followed by a whimsical one: a despot's passion is for ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase, from Pope, names the dominant motive that governs a person's whole conduct.

clue.text: Member of the opposition in Victorian times

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Talk of a member of the parliamentary opposition in the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti is a person who is against something, one of those opposing a proposal.

blocks.note: surface reading: a jealous response to someone else's luck
setter's reading: fruit too acid to be worth crushing for wine

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from Aesop's fox, who decided the grapes he could not reach were unripe anyway; 'pressing' also hints at pressing a complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names belittling something only because you cannot have it yourself, a jealous dismissal.

blocks.note: present as in the current moment
an old English measure of cloth, 45 inches

explanation.surface: A Christmas gift of an old length of material, forty-five inches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift but means the current time.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowell is an archaic spelling of Noel, the old carol word for Christmas.

blocks.note: in style
the pressed fold down a trouser leg

explanation.surface: An extra trendy pressed line down the trouser leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An increase is an addition, more of something than before.

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible version, so the letters could be set out another way

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An owner gives a pet animal sugar as a treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasturage is grazing land or grass eaten by livestock, so it is animal fodder.

clue.text: Schedule means item is thrown overboard

indicators.note: thrown means tossed about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: four letters rearranged
read as 'over board': a board, as in bed and board, is a table, and over places it below the first piece in a down entry

explanation.surface: Something is jettisoned from a ship according to a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overboard' must be split: 'over' places the first piece above the second in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable is a schedule listing when events or departures happen.

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation of the city
is means exists or lives

explanation.surface: A statement that some woman resides in Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition: a pronoun standing for any woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisa is a girl's name, so 'she' stands for a female person called that.

blocks.note: first meaning: to interrogate for information
second meaning: a device that blows up tyres

explanation.surface: An economist asks what drives rising prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To pump someone is to quiz them persistently; a pump is also the tool that forces air into tyres or balloons.

clue.text: Quietly withdraw and go before the others

blocks.note: piano, the musical direction for soft
to pull back

explanation.surface: Someone slips away quietly, leaving ahead of the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to come or go in front of others in time or order.

clue.text: Delivery secures wicket before end of the game

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so one piece is held inside another
end of picks the final letter of the next word

blocks.note: a bowler's delivery in cricket
a wicket is also a small gate
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A cricket ball takes a wicket just before the match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket surface hides the second sense of wicket, a small gate; BALL holds GATE, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: Bagatelle is a table game where balls are struck into scoring holes among pins.

clue.text: Broken treadle had a warning notice

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces that can be reassembled differently

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A faulty sewing machine pedal came with a cautionary sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alerted has been warned, given advance notice of danger.

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: classes are lessons, which sounds the same

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to teach spoken classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' looks like 'refuses', but is a verb meaning diminishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessens means reduces or diminishes, as something that declines grows smaller.

blocks.note: first meaning: a shout of 'Out!' demanding someone go
second meaning: public protest

explanation.surface: Demands that a minister step down provoke a furore.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcry is a loud public protest, a clamour of objection, often demanding someone quit.

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters run riot

blocks.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Ancient Italian riders galloping fiercely.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaurs in Greek myth are half man, half horse, literally horse-men.

blocks.note: first meaning: forgive
second meaning: let off a duty

explanation.surface: A prisoner is forgiven and set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse is to forgive a fault, and also to exempt someone from an obligation.

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for a hundred
a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Plenty of fish behave like shellfish clamped to rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: C is a hundred, a crossword convention for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpets are famous for holding fast to rocks, so to cling is to stick tightly.

blocks.note: surface reading: a forked tongue, like a snake's
setter's reading: a language whose name is hyphenated into two halves

explanation.walkthrough: The language of the former Yugoslavia is written with a hyphen, so its name is literally split.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the South Slavic language, now usually treated as separate national standards, whose two-part name joins two peoples.

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: only the first four letters of this word are fodder; the rest is the definition

explanation.surface: A clock of unusual design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timepiece' must be split: time is the fodder, piece the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single article or object, one piece among several.

clue.text: It's evenly distributed as a name for either sex

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the letters are dealt out differently

blocks.note: six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A unisex name is said to be fairly shared between the sexes.
explanation.walkthrough: Evelyn Waugh was a man; Evelyn is also a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn has been used as a given name for both boys and girls, so it suits either gender.

blocks.note: Anno Domini, the current era
long periods

explanation.surface: Proverbs from the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are proverbs, old wise sayings passed down through generations.
